note: Permanent differences no place on Earth can reproduce, and the test hardware teams use to compensate. Values are well-established approximate figures. Per-target temperature gaps are computed by the engine and stored in each scores_<target>.json under 'earth_gaps'.

gaps.label: Gravity
gaps.why_it_matters: Changes how astronauts walk, how rovers grip, and how dust settles.
how_to_fake_it: Gravity offloading rigs that carry part of a person's or rover's weight (e.g. NASA's ARGOS at Johnson Space Center)
Parabolic flights: ~20 to 30 seconds of Moon or Mars gravity per arc
Lighter test rovers built to the same ground pressure as the real one

gaps.label: Air
gaps.mars: ~600 Pa (under 1% of Earth), mostly carbon dioxide
gaps.why_it_matters: Thin or no air changes heat loss, dust behaviour, sound, drone flight and suit design.
how_to_fake_it: Thermal vacuum chambers for Moon hardware
Mars simulation chambers filled with low-pressure CO2
Earth's highest plateaus (Tibet, Atacama) for partial low-pressure and high-UV testing

detail.mars: ~600 Pa (under 1% of Earth), mostly carbon dioxide

gaps.label: Radiation
gaps.earth: ~2.4 mSv per year at the surface (shielded by air and magnetic field)
gaps.mars: ~0.67 mSv per day at the surface (Curiosity RAD), roughly 100x Earth
gaps.moon: Higher than Mars surface: no atmosphere and no magnetic field
gaps.why_it_matters: Sets mission length, habitat shielding and electronics design.
how_to_fake_it: Particle accelerator beams (e.g. NASA Space Radiation Laboratory at Brookhaven)
Testing habitat shielding concepts in caves, lava tubes and under regolith-like soils

detail.mars: ~0.67 mSv per day at the surface (Curiosity RAD), roughly 100x Earth
detail.moon: Higher than Mars surface: no atmosphere and no magnetic field
detail.earth: ~2.4 mSv per year at the surface (shielded by air and magnetic field)

gaps.source: Well-established approximate values; Mars surface radiation from Curiosity RAD (Hassler et al. 2014, Science)

gaps.label: Magnetic field
gaps.mars: No global field; patches of ancient magnetised crust
gaps.moon: No global field; weak local anomalies
gaps.why_it_matters: Affects compasses, navigation and magnetometer science.
how_to_fake_it: Helmholtz coil cages that cancel Earth's field around an instrument
Basalts with strong remnant magnetism (e.g. Iceland) for magnetometer calibration

detail.mars: No global field; patches of ancient magnetised crust
detail.moon: No global field; weak local anomalies

gaps.label: Temperature extremes
gaps.earth: Land surface roughly -64 C to +48 C (2023 yearly means, MODIS)
gaps.mars: Nights colder than anywhere on Earth; day-night swings ~55 C at Jezero
gaps.moon: +127 C day to -173 C night at the equator
gaps.why_it_matters: Batteries, seals, lubricants and materials fail at extremes.
how_to_fake_it: Antarctic and Tibetan field seasons for the coldest natural conditions
